PG.rationale: PG presents a deteriorating fundamental picture with no near-term stabilization signal. The franchise itself is durable (dominant market positions, repeat-purchase demand, 70-year dividend streak, $14.6B adjusted FCF), but the quantitative trajectory is unambiguously negative: three consecutive quarters of sequential EPS decline ($1.95→$1.78→$1.63), operating margin compression from 26.2% to 21.6% (−460bp), and OCF declining from $5.41B to $4.04B. The P/E at 22.1x is at the floor of its 365-day range, but this is not a genuine bargain — the earnings yield of 4.5% essentially matches the 10-year Treasury at 4.47%, leaving zero equity risk premium for a company whose earnings are actively declining. The market is correctly pricing in margin erosion from $1B in after-tax cost headwinds and $400M tariff impacts, with management signaling FY2026 results toward the lower end of guidance. The 7,000-job restructuring is a margin-defense measure, not a growth catalyst, and carries execution risk. At a forward P/E of ~20.7x versus the consumer staples sector average of ~17.9x, PG remains expensive relative to peers despite its deteriorating trajectory. The stock is down ~12.7% over three months while the S&P 500 gained ~10%, confirming the market is actively de-rating the name. There is no credible near-term fundamental catalyst to reverse this trend — Q4 would need to show stabilization that the data does not yet support. This is a case where a quality franchise is being correctly repriced for deteriorating economics, and the valuation floor provides no cushion.
